theme: The Prince; priestly regulations; the inheritance [survey]
readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 44:1-46:24. This is a survey day. These chapters describe the closed east gate, the rules for priests, the division of the land, and the worship of the prince and the people. Read for the main principle: worship in the restored temple is holy and ordered, and God’s people are to approach with reverence.
settingTheScene: This section follows the return of the glory in chapter 43. The details of the restored worship are laid out: who may enter, who may serve, how the festivals are to be kept. Many of the details are hard to match with any known period of Israel’s history, and Christians have understood them in different ways. The common thread is the holiness of God and the order of worship he requires.
observation: “This gate shall remain shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall enter by it, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it” (44:2).
“No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, of all the foreigners who are among the people of Israel, shall enter my sanctuary” (44:9).
“They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean” (44:23).
“I am their inheritance: you shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession” (44:28).
“The land shall be for the LORD… a holy portion” (45:1).
“My princes shall no more oppress my people” (45:8).
“You shall have just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath” (45:10).
“The people of the land shall bow down at the entrance of that gate before the LORD on the Sabbaths and on the new moons” (46:3).
interpretation:
The closed east gate is a symbol of God’s presence. The glory entered through it, so it stays shut. It is a picture of the finality of God’s return. Only the prince may sit in the gateway to eat bread before the LORD. The restored community is to be ordered around the holy.

The priests’ regulations are demanding. The Levites who went astray in idolatry are limited to lesser duties, while the sons of Zadok, who stayed faithful, may come near. The priests are to be careful in their clothing, grooming, and conduct. They are to teach the people the difference between the holy and the common, to judge disputes, and to keep the Sabbaths. In 44:28, there is a note that echoes Psalm 73: “I am their inheritance.” The priests have no land because God himself is their portion.

Chapter 45 sets aside a holy portion of land for the sanctuary, for the priests, and for the Levites, and a portion for the city and the prince. The prince is warned not to oppress the people. It is a vision of just leadership. “Enough, O princes of Israel! Put away violence and oppression.” He is to maintain just weights and measures. Worship and justice are joined.

Chapter 46 describes the offerings and worship of the prince and the people. The prince leads the people and enters with them: “When they go in, he shall go in.” He is among them, not above them. The chapter ends with the kitchens where the priests and people boil and bake the sacrifices.

For the Christian, the details are difficult. But we can see the principles. God is to be approached with reverence. The leader must be just and humble. Those who serve are to know God as their portion. And the people are to come together to worship. The New Testament shows that Christ has become our great high priest and our sacrifice, so these shadows find their fulfillment in him.
connection: Hebrews 8:1-6 and 9:11-14 show that Christ is the high priest of the true tent, and that his blood obtains eternal redemption. Hebrews 10:19-22 invites us to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus. 1 Peter 2:5, 9 calls the church a holy priesthood and a royal priesthood. Revelation 1:6 says Christ has made us a kingdom, priests to his God and Father. Romans 12:1: present your bodies as a living sacrifice.
application:
Approach worship this week with reverence. Prepare your heart before you gather.

If you lead others, ask whether you walk among them, as the prince did, or above them.

Thank God that he is your portion and inheritance, like the Levites.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that his presence is among his people.
Ask him to teach you to distinguish the holy from the common.
Ask him to guard your worship.
